title: Social participation using the AV1 robot in pediatric oncology - a pilot study
summary:
The pilot study aims to examine the use of the AV1 telepresence robot in the clinical care of children and adolescents with cancer at the University Medical Center Halle and to assess user acceptance among the children, adolescents, and their parents. Furthermore, the study will identify factors that facilitate and hinder the use of the AV1. This information is collected from the perspectives of both the children and adolescents and their families, as well as from the perspectives of the schools and the treatment team.
The AV1 avatar is a telepresence robot that enables sick children and adolescents to stay in touch with their school and classmates. In this way, it can help children who are unable to attend school due to (oncological) illnesses to participate in social and school life and improve their well-being. To date, it remains unclear how the AV1 can be integrated into hospital care services and what effects its use has, for example, on quality of life and social participation.
The findings are intended to provide insight into the everyday use of the AV1 and the experiences of the families involved as well as teachers and classmates, in order to optimize the use of the AV1 to meet their needs.
conditions: User acceptance, social participation, and quality of life associated with the use of the AV1 telepresence robot.

interventions.name: Children and adolescents with cancer use the AV1 for a period of 3 months. A questionnaire will be used to assess user acceptance among the children/adolescents and their parents both before the program begins and three months after it starts. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Cancer
- Starting from the first year of school
- Admission subject to a medical assessment of the child’s health
- Technical skills/experience using laptops, tablets, etc. (turning the tablet on and off, launching apps, using the on-screen keyboard, typing short messages)
Exclusion criteria:
None
